value.rationale: Element commutativity degree is a recently introduced finite-Lie-algebra invariant, and the primary paper itself computes a five-dimensional standard-filiform boundary case. The result promotes that isolated calculation to a complete adjoint-rank spectrum in every higher dimension and, more substantially, obtains a distinct five-stratum spectrum for the second canonical maximal-class bracket. The two exact formulas show that algebras of the same dimension and maximal nilpotency class have sharply different centralizer statistics and even different fixed-field asymptotic levels. Because the model filiform family is a canonical baseline for filiform deformations, these spectra provide natural benchmarks rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
